boards.title: Your First Weekend at Haverford College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, campus-centered sequence of places to orient yourself, eat, make, browse, and catch a public program.

cards.entity_name: Giancarlo and Maria Cristina Galdi Integrated Academic Center
cards.title: Start at the GIAC Lobby
cards.subtitle: Arrival and campus orientation
cards.notes: Use the GIAC Lobby as a recognizable first anchor, then open the College’s interactive map and identify the paths to your next few stops.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a named campus landmark and map reference.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the GIAC Lobby as the location for new-student check-in and links its campus map from arrival information.
cards.access_notes: Check the College’s arrival and campus-map information for current access details.

cards.title: Pause at Founders Hall
cards.subtitle: A historic campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk to Founders Hall and take in the building’s central place on campus; save its Great Hall programming for an event that is actually posted.
cards.short_summary: Connect the weekend route to Haverford’s original college building.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford states that Founders Hall was built in 1833, originally housed the entire college, and includes Founders Great Hall for events.
cards.access_notes: Administrative and event spaces may have limited access; view current event listings before entering program areas.

cards.title: Find the original swamp white oak
cards.subtitle: Lloyd Green, between Founders Hall and Marshall Auditorium
cards.notes: Make this one tree your arboretum introduction: locate it on Lloyd Green, observe its canopy, and use the Arboretum Explorer for more labeled specimens.
cards.short_summary: A specific living landmark from the original landscape plan.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum identifies an original swamp white oak on Lloyd Green between Founders Hall and Marshall Auditorium.
cards.source_title: Haverford College's Original Oaks | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus and landscape guidance.

cards.title: Walk down to Duck Pond
cards.subtitle: Arboretum highlight
cards.notes: Continue downhill for a short outdoor reset at Duck Pond, then look toward Roberts Hall and the surrounding meadow before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A named pond with a documented student-and-community history.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford documents Duck Pond as a year-round campus feature used by students and the community, with the historic skate house still present.
cards.access_notes: Stay on maintained paths and observe posted pond-area guidance.

cards.title: Take a section of the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Arboretum perimeter route
cards.notes: Choose a daylight section rather than attempting the full route; the trail passes conifers, meadows, fields, woodlands, and the campus ponds.
cards.short_summary: A flexible walking leg through the College Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford says its 2.2-mile Nature Trail roughly follows the campus perimeter and passes through arboretum collections, meadows, fields, woodlands, and ponds.
cards.access_notes: Use during daylight and follow posted conditions; trail surfaces and maintenance can vary.

cards.title: Plan a weekend meal at the Dining Center
cards.subtitle: Campus dining
cards.notes: Check the current menu and hours before heading over; Saturday service is listed for breakfast, brunch, light lunch, and dinner.
cards.short_summary: A practical food stop with officially published weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s Dining Center page lists Saturday breakfast, brunch, light lunch, and dinner service.
cards.source_title: Dining Center | Haverford College Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Hours and meal service can change; consult the Dining Center page or posted updates before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into Lutnick Library
cards.subtitle: Library study and research spaces
cards.notes: Use this stop to get familiar with the main library’s study options, service points, café, and reservable rooms before coursework gets busy.
cards.short_summary: A named library with study, technology, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists study rooms, reservable carrels, computers, scanners, a café, and research support at Lutnick Library.
cards.access_notes: Current building and visitor hours are published by the Libraries; some rooms require reservations.

cards.title: Browse the Cantor Fitzgerald Gallery
cards.subtitle: Whitehead Campus Center, first floor
cards.notes: See what exhibition is currently installed, then use the gallery’s directions page to navigate from the Campus Center entrance or elevator.
cards.short_summary: A campus exhibition stop with published weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official directions page places it on the first floor of Whitehead Campus Center and lists Saturday–Sunday hours of noon–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed weekend hours are noon–5 p.m.; confirm the current exhibition and any closures before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media Building
cards.title: Look into VCAM programming
cards.subtitle: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media
cards.notes: Stop by the VCAM Building and check its public programs or exhibitions; ask staff about workshops and maker opportunities that fit your interests.
cards.short_summary: A creative hub for visual studies, arts, media, and making.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes VCAM as a creative hub housing visual studies, maker arts, the Hurford Center, and the Haverford Innovations Program.
cards.source_title: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media VCAM | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: The College describes VCAM as a 24/7 hub, but individual studios, equipment, and programs can have eligibility or scheduling requirements.

cards.title: End with a Roberts Hall program
cards.subtitle: Music and performance venue
cards.notes: Check the Department of Music calendar and choose a posted concert or talk in Roberts Hall; arrive for the actual listed start time.
cards.short_summary: A final event-oriented stop anchored by campus performance spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford states that public concerts are held in Michael Jaharis Recital Hall and Marshall Auditorium in Roberts Hall.
cards.access_notes: Attend only events listed on the College calendar; ticketing, start times, and access vary by program.
